problems.title: Two Sum
problems.statement: Return indices of two distinct elements whose values sum to target. Return [-1, -1] if no pair exists.
problems.constraints: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; values and target fit signed 32-bit integers.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) space
problems.common_mistakes: Using the same element twice; returning values instead of indices; failing with duplicate values.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.statement: Return true if two strings contain exactly the same characters with the same frequencies.
problems.constraints: Strings contain lowercase English letters; lengths up to 200000.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space for fixed alphabet
problems.common_mistakes: Checking only set equality; ignoring character counts; not checking length.

problems.title: First Non-Repeating Character
problems.statement: Return the index of the first character that occurs exactly once, or -1 if none exists.
problems.constraints: String length up to 200000; lowercase English letters.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space for fixed alphabet
problems.common_mistakes: Returning the character rather than its index; returning the first character without counting all occurrences.

problems.title: Move Zeroes
problems.statement: Move all zeroes to the end while preserving the relative order of non-zero elements. Modify and return the array.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space
problems.common_mistakes: Sorting the array; changing the order of non-zero elements; allocating unnecessary arrays when in-place behavior is required.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.statement: Return the index of target in a sorted ascending array, or -1 if absent.
problems.constraints: Array length up to 1000000; values may repeat; return any matching index.
problems.complexity: O(log n) time, O(1) space
problems.common_mistakes: Using an incorrect loop condition; forgetting absent targets; computing midpoint as (left+right) in fixed-width languages.

problems.title: Merge Sorted Arrays
problems.statement: Return a sorted array containing all elements from two sorted arrays.
problems.constraints: Each array length up to 100000.
problems.complexity: O(n+m) time, O(n+m) output space
problems.common_mistakes: Appending remaining tail incorrectly; assuming unique values; using repeated sorting instead of linear merge.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray Sum
problems.statement: Return the maximum sum of any non-empty contiguous subarray.
problems.constraints: 1 <= len(nums) <= 200000; values can be negative.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space
problems.common_mistakes: Initializing best sum to zero, which fails when all values are negative; resetting the running sum at the wrong time.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.statement: Given daily prices, return the maximum profit from one buy followed by one later sell. Return 0 if no profit is possible.
problems.constraints: 1 <= len(prices) <= 200000; prices are non-negative.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space
problems.common_mistakes: Selling before buying; allowing multiple transactions; failing to handle monotonically decreasing prices.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeats
problems.statement: Return the length of the longest substring with no repeated characters.
problems.constraints: String length up to 200000; arbitrary Unicode characters.
problems.complexity: O(n) expected time, O(k) space
problems.common_mistakes: Moving the left boundary backwards when a duplicate was seen earlier; confusing substring with subsequence.

problems.title: Balanced Brackets
problems.statement: Return true when (), [], and {} brackets are correctly nested and matched; other characters do not occur.
problems.constraints: String length up to 200000.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) space
problems.common_mistakes: Checking only counts rather than nesting order; popping an empty stack; accepting leftover opening brackets.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.statement: Return the k most frequent values. If frequencies tie, smaller numeric values must appear first.
problems.constraints: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; 1 <= k <= number of distinct values.
problems.complexity: O(n log n) time with sorting distinct values; O(n) space
problems.common_mistakes: Not defining tie behavior; returning duplicates; assuming input values are positive.

problems.title: Product Except Self
problems.statement: Return an array where each position is the product of all other elements, without using division.
problems.constraints: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000; products fit signed 64-bit integer.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space excluding output
problems.common_mistakes: Using division despite the requirement; mishandling zero values; forgetting prefix or suffix product updates.

problems.title: Rotate Array Right
problems.statement: Rotate an array right by k positions and return the resulting array.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) output space
problems.common_mistakes: Forgetting k modulo n; failing on empty arrays; rotating left instead of right.

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.statement: An array contains n distinct values from 0 through n with one value missing. Return the missing value.
problems.constraints: 0 <= len(nums) <= 100000; values are distinct and in [0,n].
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space
problems.common_mistakes: Assuming values start at 1; using an incorrect range endpoint; integer overflow in languages with narrow integer types.

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.statement: Group strings that are anagrams. The order of groups and members does not matter.
problems.constraints: 1 <= number of strings <= 10000; total characters <= 200000.
problems.complexity: O(total characters * log(max word length)) time; O(total characters) space
problems.common_mistakes: Using a key that loses character counts; assuming input has no empty strings; comparing groups in a fixed order.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.statement: Given a rectangular grid of '1' and '0', count connected groups of land using 4-directional adjacency.
problems.constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 300.
problems.complexity: O(rows * cols) time, O(rows * cols) worst-case space
problems.common_mistakes: Counting each land cell as an island; using diagonal adjacency; revisiting cells indefinitely.

problems.title: Shortest Path in Unweighted Graph
problems.statement: Given an undirected graph with n vertices labeled 0..n-1 and edges, return the shortest number of edges from source to target, or -1 if unreachable.
problems.constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000; graph is unweighted.
problems.complexity: O(V+E) time, O(V+E) space
problems.common_mistakes: Using DFS and assuming the first found path is shortest; forgetting disconnected vertices; adding duplicate edges is harmless but can waste time.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.statement: Count ways to reach step n when each move is 1 or 2 steps.
problems.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space
problems.common_mistakes: Wrong base cases; confusing Fibonacci indexing; returning zero for n=0 when the empty sequence counts as one way.

problems.title: Coin Change Minimum
problems.statement: Return the minimum number of coins needed to make amount, or -1 if impossible. Coins can be reused unlimited times.
problems.complexity: O(amount * number of coin types) time, O(amount) space
problems.common_mistakes: Greedy choice fails for arbitrary coin systems; treating unreachable states as zero; not handling amount=0.

problems.title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
problems.statement: Merge all overlapping intervals and return non-overlapping intervals sorted by start. Touching endpoints count as overlapping.
problems.constraints: 0 <= number of intervals <= 100000; start <= end.
problems.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) output space
problems.common_mistakes: Not sorting first; treating touching endpoints as separate; mutating interval endpoints incorrectly.

problems.title: Customers Without Orders
problems.statement: Return customer IDs and names for customers who have never placed an order.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.schema: customers(customer_id, name); orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount)
problems.reference_solution: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.customer_id;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: LEFT JOIN plus IS NULL or NOT EXISTS; avoid NOT IN if the subquery may contain NULL.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Revenue by Region
problems.statement: Return each region and total order revenue, including only regions with revenue above 1000.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.schema: customers(customer_id, name, region); orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount)
problems.reference_solution: SELECT c.region, SUM(o.amount) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.region HAVING SUM(o.amount) > 1000 ORDER BY revenue DESC;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: Filter aggregated results with HAVING, not WHERE.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Second Highest Salary
problems.statement: Return the second-highest distinct salary, or NULL if it does not exist.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.reference_solution: SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_highest_salary FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: Distinct salary levels matter; MAX below the maximum handles ties.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Top Employee per Department
problems.statement: Return all employees tied for the highest salary in each department.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.reference_solution: WITH ranked AS (SELECT e.*, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk FROM employees e) SELECT employee_id, name, department_id, salary FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY department_id, employee_id;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: Use DENSE_RANK or RANK to preserve ties; ROW_NUMBER returns only one winner.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Monthly Revenue
problems.statement: Return monthly revenue grouped by year and month. Ignore rows with NULL amount.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.reference_solution: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE amount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) ORDER BY month;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: This reference uses SQLite strftime; date syntax varies by database.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Duplicate Emails
problems.statement: Return email addresses that occur more than once. Ignore NULL email values.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.reference_solution: SELECT email FROM users WHERE email IS NOT NULL GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY email;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: Use COUNT(*) after excluding NULLs; grouping by user_id would defeat duplicate detection.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Customers With At Least Three Orders
problems.statement: Return each customer ID and name for customers with at least three orders.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.schema: customers(customer_id, name); orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount)
problems.reference_solution: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 3 ORDER BY c.customer_id;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: COUNT orders, not amount; aggregate by customer identity.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Running Account Balance
problems.statement: For each account transaction, return transaction ID, account ID, date, amount, and running balance. Order same-day transactions by transaction_id.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.reference_solution: SELECT transaction_id, account_id, transaction_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY transaction_date, transaction_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_balance FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id, transaction_date, transaction_id;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: Include a deterministic tie-breaker and explicit ROWS frame.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Products Never Sold
problems.statement: Return product IDs and names for products that do not appear in any order item.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.reference_solution: SELECT p.product_id, p.name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id) ORDER BY p.product_id;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: A product can exist without sales; NOT EXISTS avoids NULL pitfalls.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.

problems.title: Daily Active Users
problems.statement: Return each date and count of distinct users who performed at least one event that day.
problems.constraints: Use the schema listed below. Unless stated otherwise, return only the requested columns.
problems.reference_solution: SELECT date(event_time) AS event_date, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS active_users FROM events WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY date(event_time) ORDER BY event_date;
problems.complexity: Depends on indexes and database query plan; discuss scans, joins, grouping, and sorting.
problems.common_mistakes: Count distinct users rather than events; date truncation depends on SQL dialect.
test_cases: Create data for empty tables, duplicate keys, NULL values, ties, and boundary dates as relevant.
